title: Rickey Dixon: First Sooner to Win the Jim Thorpe Award
question: Who was the first Oklahoma player to win the Jim Thorpe Award?
answer: Safety Rickey Dixon was the first Sooner to win the Jim Thorpe Award, sharing the 1987 honor with Miami's Bennie Blades. He set OU's single-season record with nine interceptions that year.
summary: Rickey Dixon became the first Sooner to win the Jim Thorpe Award in 1987, sharing it with Miami's Bennie Blades after a school-record nine interceptions.
body: The Jim Thorpe Award is voted on by an Oklahoma City organization, so it is fitting that a Sooner made history with it early on. In 1987 safety Rickey Dixon became the first Oklahoma player to win the award, which honors the nation's top defensive back. He shared it with Miami's Bennie Blades.

Dixon's senior season was a ball-hawking clinic. He picked off nine passes, a school single-season record, and led the Big Eight in interceptions. He was a consensus All-American that year and a first-team All-Big Eight selection in both 1986 and 1987, and he was named Big Eight Defensive Player of the Week four times in 1987.

His signature moment came in the 1987 showdown billed as Game of the Century II, with No. 1 Nebraska hosting No. 2 Oklahoma. Dixon intercepted two Husker passes, the second in the fourth quarter, helping seal a 17-7 road win and an Orange Bowl berth.

The Dallas native finished his career with 17 interceptions, a Big Eight record and second-most in OU history, plus 303 interception return yards. Oklahoma went 42-5-1 across his four seasons and played in the Orange Bowl every year, including the 1985 national championship team he helped as a sophomore.

The Cincinnati Bengals drafted Dixon fifth overall in 1988, and he played in Super Bowl XXIII. In 2019 he became OU's first full-time defensive back in the College Football Hall of Fame. Dixon passed away in August 2020 at age 53.
